transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-29
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Lucas Patel (Redwood SE), Ravi Kumar (Head of ML, AuroraTech), Sophie Martin (Platform Engineer), Carlos Diaz (CTO)
Links shared: https://redwood.app/poc/auroratech-deck , https://redwood.app/poc/auroratech-benchmark-template.xlsx , security packet: https://redwood.app/security/soc2

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for making time, quick round intro and then jump into the workload stuff.
[00:15] Ravi Kumar: Hi all, Ravi here. We're looking to validate an LLM-based claims triage and summary pipeline, so main focus is latency under peak, and cost.
[00:25] Sophie Martin: Sophie, infra, I'll own the sample traces and will coordinate infra access.
[00:30] Lucas Patel: Lucas from Redwood, I'll run the workload modeling and the benchmarks, go over configs with you.
[00:40] Carlos Diaz: Carlos - high level, timeline is Q3 pilot then decide in Q4.

Summary / Goals 
[01:05] Maya: Quick recap of what we want from today - QPS and concurrency targets, token distributions for the two main flows (triage/classification + summary), define bench plan and success criteria, and lock a POC start date.

Traffic characterization discussion
[02:00] Ravi: Current production traffic for claims intake is about 8 qps on avg, spikes up to 60 qps during batch uploads; for the triage microservice we expect between 10-40 qps typical with 90th percentile bursts to ~80 qps. We're planning to start POC on a 10k customer slice.
[02:30] Lucas: Ok that's helpful. Do you have concurrency numbers - how many simultaneous requests typically?
[02:40] Sophie: For triage the concurrency map is variable - usually 3-6 concurrent per worker, but during peak the front-end fans out so we see up to 40 concurrent inference requests across the cluster.
[03:05] Maya: Good, we should model both steady-state QPS (10-15) and burst profile (60-80) and run benchmarks at both.

Token distributions and payloads
[04:00] Ravi: For triage the average input is short, about 60 tokens (free-text claim description, metadata). Output is a classification label plus short rationale, roughly 20-30 tokens. For the summary flow the input is whole claim notes ~300-800 tokens average 420, output summary ~60-120 tokens.
[04:35] Lucas: So two workloads - low token / low latency critical (triage) and high token / more tolerant latency (summary). We'll need different model configs or variants for each.
[05:00] Sophie: Note that our tokenization is English heavy but with some Spanish in region LATAM, token counts vary a bit. Also we have a small number of very long docs (2-3% > 2k tokens).

Latency SLOs and expectations
[06:00] Carlos: For triage we want p95 < 800ms ideally, p50 around 200-300ms. For summary p95 can be up to 2s. Cost is a big lever though — if latency for triage is much higher on hosted we might consider Dedicated.
[06:25] Maya: We can profile both. Redwood will measure p50/p95, tail latency with KV/prefix cache on vs off, and with batching tuned. Expect some tradeoffs: batching improves throughput but can add headroom to latency.
[06:50] Ravi: Agree, also want to understand warm vs cold token costs, and caching benefit on repeated prefixes.

Benchmarking approach
[07:20] Lucas: Proposed bench plan: 1) baseline run with customer's sample traces (token distribution preserved) at steady QPS 15, burst 80 for 30mins each; 2) run quantized model variants (8-bit/4-bit where available) and batching configs; 3) measure cost per 1M tokens, p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput and peak concurrency behavior. We'll include a KV cache experiment to show cache hit improvements.
[08:00] Sophie: Does Redwood simulate client-side retry/backoff patterns? Our frontend does exponential backoff so saw microbursts that create tail load.
[08:20] Lucas: Yes we can mirror retry/backoff in the synthetic generator; please send a sample trace with timestamps.

Data & security constraints
[09:00] Sophie: Data residency is EU-first, we need KMS integration and audit logs. SOC2 and ISO docs will be required — can't do a hosted POC on US-only infra without legal signoff.
[09:20] Maya: Understood. For the POC we can offer Dedicated or Private. For initial bench we can do a Redwood-hosted isolated tenant in eu-west, and if that isn't acceptable, we can spin up a Private deployment in your VPC. We'll attach SOC2 packet and KMS integration guide.
[09:45] Carlos: Also need SAML SSO and RBAC for the console.
[09:50] Maya: We'll include those in the security packet link.

Success criteria (customer-driven)
[10:30] Ravi: Our proposed success criteria: 1) triage p95 < 800ms under steady+burst profile, 2) summary p95 < 2s, 3) cost delta less than 30% vs our current hosted vendor for equivalent output quality, 4) no more than 2% accuracy regression on classification labels vs baseline.
[11:00] Maya: Sounds reasonable. We'll also propose Redwood's own pass/fail thresholds for the bench and make sure measurement methodology is transparent.

POC duration and milestones
[12:00] Lucas: Typical POC is 4 weeks: week 0 - prep & infra + sample traces; week 1 - baseline benchmark + verify telemetry; week 2 - optimization (quant, batching, cache); week 3 - soak tests and handoff + run runbook and handover.
[12:30] Sophie: Timeline fits Q3 pilot ask. Can we target start week of 2026-08-10?
[12:40] Maya: We proposed initial start earlier but with security gating, realistic start is Aug 10. We'll aim for SOW sign off by Aug 5.

Technical details / preferred models and infra
[13:20] Ravi: We're open to open models. Current internal evals used a Llama-variant and a small proprietary masked model for classification. We care about FP16 vs quantized tradeoffs.
[13:40] Lucas: For triage we might recommend a smaller low-latency model (e.g., 13B quantized) to meet p95 targets; for summary a larger 70B or 33B may be required if quality gap shows up. We'll propose a model matrix for the POC.
[14:00] Carlos: For Dedicated we need guaranteed throughput 500k tokens/hour at peak - what's the expected GPU footprint?
[14:20] Lucas: Rough ballpark: a quantized 13B optimized runtime can handle ~120-180 qps depending on seq length and batching on a single A10G-ish instance; larger models scale down QPS. We'll provide exact perf numbers in the benchmark report.

Workload modeling numbers agreed
[15:00] Maya: Recap the numbers we should model: steady QPS 10-15, concurrency 3-6 per worker, burst spikes up to 80 QPS system-wide, triage median input 60 tokens output 25 tokens, summary input median 420 tokens output 90 tokens, tail docs 2-3% >2k tokens.
[15:30] Ravi: Correct. Also model retries that add ~15% extra requests during peak windows.

Artifacts and measurement details
[16:00] Lucas: We'll need: sample traces (timestamps, payload sizes), representative prompt templates, target traffic shaping script (we'll provide), and the quality evaluation set for classification labels. Please upload to the shared drive.
[16:20] Sophie: I'll upload traces and token distribution CSV by Aug 4.
[16:30] Maya: We'll share a benchmark config YAML and the synthetic traffic generator with default retry/backoff patterns.

Discussion: caching, KV & prefix caching
[17:00] Lucas: For the summary flow, prefix caching probably won't help; for triage we expect high reuse of phrases and claim templates so KV/prefix cache can cut tokens and latency. We'll report cache hit rate impact.
[17:30] Ravi: Any caveats around correctness when caching? We occasionally need fresh context and can't serve stale responses.
[17:40] Lucas: We'll show hit/miss analysis and how to invalidate cache on metadata changes.

Commercials & pricing
[18:30] Carlos: Pricing sensitivity: we need to see cost per 1M tokens for baseline and quantized runs, and expected monthly run-rate for pilot scale.
[18:45] Maya: We'll include both hosted metered pricing and Dedicated reserved pricing scenarios in SOW. Also show unit economics with and without caching.

Open questions / Risks
[19:30] Sophie: Risk: sample traces might not capture peak concurrency patterns; need to ensure we model those correctly.
[19:45] Lucas: Agreed - ask for 30 days of traces including a burst day.
[19:55] Ravi: Legal review of data residency may push to Private deployment which extends timeline.
[20:05] Maya: Noted; will flag in SOW.

Recap & next steps
[20:45] Maya: Recap: Redwood to send SOW/pricing by Aug 5; Sophie to upload traces by Aug 4; Lucas to run baseline bench and share initial results by Aug 14; follow-up call to review benchmarks week of Aug 17.
[21:10] Carlos: Fine by us.

Closing
[21:30] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and a calendar invite for the bench review.
[21:40] Ravi: Thanks.

Notes: Transcript auto-generated; some speaker boundaries may be off; occasional transcription artifacts (e.g., K V cache vs KV cache, model names garbled).
